explanation: The word "but" signals that Luo's research contradicts the idea in the blank. Luo found that early mammals weren't all ground-dwelling insectivores; some ate plants and some could glide. That shows variety, so the earlier view must have been that mammals were not very diverse. "Obscure" and "localized" aren't what the fossil evidence about varied lifestyles disproves.

Every sentence traces how jazz tap came about and changed: its origins, its influence from jazz music, and how it evolved into a distinct form. So the purpose is to discuss the development of a dance form. The text mentions music, but it never compares audience preferences, explains playing an instrument, or focuses on a single famous dancer.

The next sentence explains that most writers prefer working alone and that working together cost Hurston and Hughes their friendship. A play written by two authors is therefore an example of collaboration, which is rare in literature. "Characterization" and "interpretation" don't connect to the idea of writers working together.

Because the meteorites' isotopic signatures match Mars's atmosphere, it is tempting to treat the meteorites' properties as stand-ins for those of Mars's interior, which is what "proxies for" means. The warning that geology can't be known from meteorites alone confirms this. "Catalysts of" (causes of) and "contrivances of" (artificial creations of) don't describe using one thing to represent another.

The delays will extend the projection's time frame but are unlikely to prove it completely wrong, which is what "invalidate" means here. "Dispute" is tempting, but delays are events, not people, so they can't argue against a claim; "underscore" would mean the delays support the projection, which contradicts "challenged."

The underlined sentence says the map shows vast topographic knowledge and backs this up with specifics: named mountains and rivers and the first-known sketch of the Missouri's drainage network. These are reasons the map is impressive. The tribes are mentioned only in the following sentence, so choice A doesn't describe the underlined sentence.

Sumner helped found Howard University's psychology department, showing that he actively worked to increase opportunities for Black students. Someone who supports and advances a cause is a "proponent of" it. "Beneficiary of" is tempting, but the text shows him creating opportunities for others, not receiving them.

The broken area let Schoenemann see the inner structure of the trilobite's eye, so it provided, or offered, fresh insight. This is the surprising contrast with the idea that a damaged fossil gives less information. A fossil can't "resolve," "adjust," or "direct" insight in this context.

The text opens by saying it has been unclear how forests along streams affect stream biodiversity, then describes Giam's study that investigated exactly that question and its results. So it presents a study addressing an unresolved question. Choice C is tempting because predators are mentioned, but the text doesn't describe challenging any earlier view about how fish avoid predators.

The second sentence calls these portraits "characteristic works" and "esteemed," meaning Edwards is known for painting notable people. Being known for something is having a "reputation for" it. Nothing suggests he complains about, questions, or is required to paint these portraits.

The text first characterizes moral philosophy as concerned with how to live a good life, naming Plato's and Aristotle's works as examples. It then notes Barnes's point about works that give a method without a motive, and ends by saying some works also give reasons to live morally, making them more comprehensive. Choice B is wrong because the text never says the two named works fail their purpose or discusses their popularity.

The previous sentence makes a general claim: industrial activity isn't always a threat to wildlife. The underlined phrase introduces the silver-studded blue butterfly, which thrives in active quarries, as a specific example backing up that claim. It doesn't challenge an assumption about the butterfly itself or define a term.

Anne joyfully gushes about October and the colorful maple branches, while Marilla dismisses them as "messy things" and says bedrooms are for sleeping. The scene's purpose is to contrast their very different personalities. Choice A fails because nothing suggests Anne's love of nature is new, and choice B fails because the text shows a single exchange, not an argument they often have.

Unpredictable shifts in cloud cover and haze would make solar energy collection rise and fall, and stored energy would help smooth out those changes. "Fluctuations in" describes exactly this kind of up-and-down variation. "Developments of" and "incentives for" aren't problems caused by clouds that storage would need to mitigate.

Switching strategies when one fails is described as sophisticated, so the finding shows single-celled organisms may be capable of more than simple, basic behaviors. "Rudimentary" means basic or undeveloped, which contrasts with "sophisticatedly." "Aggressive" and "advantageous" don't set up that contrast.

Most of the passage shows how Charlot gets the letter to Rinaldo using a split cane, and then it describes his joy ("never was man so transported with joy") on reading it. That matches describing a delivery and then a character's happiness. Choice C fails because the letter's contents are never given, and choice D fails because the text doesn't explain what inspired the letter.

Text 2 accepts that the bees may play and possibly feel something positive, but stresses that insect emotions, if they exist, are likely very rudimentary. So its author would likely say any fun the bees experienced was probably quite basic. Choice A is wrong because Text 2 mentions stress only in other studies and doesn't deny the positive state shown in this one.

The text begins with the concern that pteropod shells are vulnerable to ocean acidification, then reports that the periostracum prevents dissolution and that pteropods can even rebuild damaged shells. These findings suggest the concern may be overstated. Choice B reverses the relationship: the periostracum protects the calcium carbonate shell, not the other way around.

The underlined sentence says many fossil studies of turtle relationships used incomplete data sets, which is a weakness, or limitation, of those studies. This sets up Simões's larger study, which agreed with the genetic results. The sentence doesn't criticize genetic studies or describe fossil-examination tools.

The consensus in Text 1 is that curiosity is a drive to get information purely for its own sake. Dubey's team found that presenting research as useful increased interest, which suggests usefulness also drives curiosity, not just the desire for information. Choice D goes too far, since Text 2 acknowledges that acquiring information is a powerful motivator.

Text 1's conventional wisdom says social systems moved step by step from equal bands to hierarchies to states. Graeber and Wengrow argue humans have always switched back and forth between hierarchical and collective systems, even seasonally, which disputes the idea of a linear progression through stages. Choice C is wrong because their evidence shows hunter-gatherer communities that included esteemed individuals long before agriculture.

Text 1 reports Wang's finding of mammoth eDNA from about 4 kyr ago and then Miller and Simpson's explanation that a surface carcass could leach DNA for millennia. Text 2 adds that remains would have to stay on the surface for that long, yet scavengers and weathering would destroy them within a thousand years, casting doubt on that explanation. Choice C is wrong because Miller and Simpson offer an explanation of the findings, not a critique of Wang's method.

The researchers tested whether false memories come from people having seen wrong versions of images before, and the end of the sentence restates this as "familiarity with erroneous versions." Having seen something is "exposure to" it. "Compliance with" and "criteria for" don't describe having encountered an image.

The cities are establishing reward points and incentives, which means they are setting up, or instituting, programs. "Encountering" and "occupying" don't describe creating a program, and "underestimating" doesn't fit cities that actively encourage the behavior.

Osmond's behavior is a carefully planned pose, and everything he does is "for a purpose." Living in the land of "consideration" therefore means living by careful planning, or calculation. "Deference" and "courtesy" are other meanings of the word but don't match a man whose every action is strategic.

The next sentence says the Mexica could "precisely identify" the dates of solstices, so they tracked time with a high degree of accuracy, or exactitude. "Precariousness" means instability and "inconspicuousness" means being hard to notice, neither of which fits precise timekeeping.

The vase is "marked at about twelve or fourteen dollars," so "marked" refers to the price shown on it; it means priced. "Stained" and "watched" are other meanings of "marked" that don't fit a dollar amount.

After explaining why adapting the story was hard (the story had silent thoughts but theater needs dialogue), the underlined sentence tells how Yamauchi solved this problem by having characters speak their thoughts aloud. It explains how she adapted the story into a play. Nothing in the text discusses later playwrights, casting, or which work is better known.

The narrator says there's a chance she'll make the team and then gives her reasons: she's quick, wiry, and tough, and can dodge under taller players to grab the ball. The text's purpose is to explain why she thinks she might make it. It doesn't explain how players are chosen or how to play the game.

Text 1 says scholars neglect food writing, pay the least attention to cookbooks, and especially overlook regional US cookbooks. Lewis's book is a regional Southern cookbook, so its being ignored by scholars is exactly what Text 1's author would expect. Choice A is wrong because Text 1 never says scholars dismiss works for being popular.

The sentence contrasts commentators who praised political blogs with others who warned that the blogs fueled harmful polarization. Those critics were less optimistic, and "sanguine" means optimistic or hopeful. "Recalcitrant" (stubbornly uncooperative) and "misanthropic" (disliking people) don't describe the contrast with the praising commentators.

The wind is described as "not a rough wind" but one with "delightful little gusts," so "rough" means strong and unpleasant, or harsh. "Scratchy" describes a texture, which doesn't fit wind, and "basic" and "vague" don't contrast with gentle gusts.

The speaker describes summer as a pause, a "silent space" when inspiration lags and feeling sleeps. "A void" therefore means an empty space. "A useless" is too negative, since the speaker says this time gathers strength for future efforts.

Throughout the poem, Night is described as a person: she wears a garment, draws a veil over her face, has black hair, and moves her hands. This is an extended comparison of night to a human being. The poem never shifts to sunrise, a rural setting, or changing seasons.

Jemisin is willing to thwart expectations and avoid formulaic plots, so she declines to follow the genre's conventions, which is what "conform to" means. Saying she declines to "question" the conventions would mean she accepts them, the opposite of what the text describes.

The examples show black swan families taking varied forms: successful pairs foster other pairs' young, and both female-male and male-male pairs raise cygnets. This flexibility is "elasticity." "Reciprocity" is tempting, but the text describes one-way fostering rather than an exchange between pairs, and "cohesion" would stress unity rather than variety.

The evidence offered is the great number and variety of crops the Inca grew, which shows the terrace method worked well, or was effective. "Burdensome" and "chaotic" are negative and aren't supported by that success, and "uniform" conflicts with the variety of crops.

After the colon, the text says nearly a dozen of Delany's characters are poets or writers, so being a poet is common in his work, not unusual. "Not atypical" means typical, which matches. Whether the job is "lucrative" or "tedious" isn't addressed by the count of poet characters.

The 1970s writing is contrasted with earlier stories "whose politics were less deliberately signaled," so the later feminist writing was openly and deliberately political, or "overtly" feminist. "Inadvertently" means accidentally, the opposite of deliberate, and "prudently" and "cordially" don't relate to how openly politics are signaled.

The forests slow down rough currents, creating calmer waters where animals can shelter, so the environment is peaceful, or tranquil. "Dangerous" contradicts the idea of a safe shelter, and "imaginative" and "surprising" don't describe calm water.

The text says taxes have almost no effect on moving decisions while jobs, housing, and climate are strong influences, so those other factors outweigh, or overshadow, taxes. "Irrelevant to" is tempting, but taxes aren't unrelated to the other factors; they're just less important than them.

The shop owner grumbles that the picture doesn't belong in his shop, yet he is "secretly proud" of it, with a "hidden dignity" in his scowling. The text's purpose is to show these mixed, conflicted feelings. He never expresses resentment toward the young man who sold it, so choice B is wrong.

The text reports a team's findings that the birds choose fruit by beak size at geographic boundaries but are driven more by competition at elevation boundaries. So it presents findings about how location within the range affects feeding patterns. Choice D wrongly claims the text ranks boundaries above beak size in general, and the text doesn't discuss research methods.

The underlined portion admits that public bathhouses served mainly town dwellers, meaning not everyone had access to them, before the sentence argues that people everywhere still bathed in other ways. That's a concession. It says nothing about steam baths being more popular in rural areas or about earlier historians' limitations.

The example that follows shows that light through a tree's leaves inspired Thomas's broken brushstrokes, so the garden shaped, or influenced, her work. "Restricted" and "distracted" are negative and contradict the idea of inspiration, and "announced" doesn't make sense here.

Klein used blur and distortion, which were generally seen as flaws, and his work was so unorthodox he struggled to find a publisher. That means he went against, or defied, photography's conventions. "Respected" says the opposite, and "reviewed" doesn't capture breaking the rules.

The underlined sentence says the stranger's oddness invited a closer look, and the sentences that follow deliver that close look: his lean figure, matted hair, sunken eyes, and dripping clothes. So it sets up the detailed character description that follows. The previous sentence only gives his position in the room, so the underlined sentence doesn't elaborate on or contrast with a description there.

The text notes that little is known about juvenile sea turtles' oceanic stage and then summarizes a tagging study of that stage and its results. That is a summary of research on an understudied stage. Choice D is too narrow: the reason two turtles swam against currents is mentioned only briefly as a possibility.

The underlined portion spells out Ivancevic's hypothesis step by step: a parasite picks up a gene from one vertebrate host and passes it to a host of another species. That describes a possible way horizontal gene transfer could happen among vertebrates. It doesn't compare vertebrates with invertebrates or explain why parasites resist gene transfer.

The text explains how Derksen combines Indigenous and classical music, using Orchestral Powwow as an example where an orchestra follows a powwow drum instead of a conductor. Its purpose is to examine how her music blends cultures. It doesn't argue she invented a new style or describe production difficulties.

A coin from 337 to 341 CE and building materials from that era support the idea that the amphitheater dates to the fourth century, so the discoveries provide evidence for the theory. "Dismiss" and "refuse" would mean the evidence works against the theory, which doesn't fit.

Jeyifous photographed the now-adult models and layered the photos over images of their cells, which means he made, or created, new images. "Restored" would mean repairing old images, but these are described as new ones.

Madhusudhan's team placed K2-18 b right at the inner edge of the habitable zone using models that start the zone near 1 AU. Tsai's team argues that hydrogen-rich atmospheres heat the surface and evaporate water, pushing the inner edge out to 3.85 AU, so K2-18 b would be too close and too hot to keep liquid surface water. Choices B and D get this backwards: Tsai suggests earlier temperature estimates were too low and the planet is too close, not too far.

The text calls the exhibit "essential viewing," so it would be a mistake to miss or ignore it, which is what "overlook" means. "Assemble" doesn't fit because Baker already organized it, and "amplify" wouldn't be a mistake.

"This" refers back to Franklin being very popular in France. High regard from others is "esteem." "Thoughtfulness" and "sincerity" describe Franklin's own qualities rather than how the French viewed him, and "controversy" contradicts popularity.

Text 1 says tropical mountain birds are limited to specific elevations because of temperature, and Text 2 says competition, not temperature, limits where they live. They disagree on the cause, but both agree these birds are restricted in where they can live. Neither text discusses tools, nests, or genetics.

The text explains that the tough soil crust keeps seeds from germinating, and the underlined portion shows how nesting birds help: by churning the soil, they expose buried seeds to moisture and nutrients. That explains how the birds promote germination. It doesn't describe how seeds get into the soil or why the birds dig nests.

Moss never tires of "this specific view," meaning the one particular view of the Port of Oakland seen from the elevated track. "Particular" fits. "Correct" is a different sense that doesn't apply to a view.

The word "but" sets up a contrast with Bastos's finding that the kea used the stones "deliberately." The skeptics must have suggested the opposite, that the interactions were accidental. "Intriguing" and "observable" don't contrast with deliberate use.

Text 1 notes that Lewis sculpted historical and mythical figures as well as other subjects, and Text 2 says she made both historical sculptures and many portrait busts. Both authors would agree her work covered varied subjects. Choice A contradicts both texts, since Text 2 says the busts have been ignored.

Francie plans to read every book in the library in alphabetical order, one a day, without skipping the dry ones, and keeps going even though some B's were "hard going." The text's purpose is to show her determination to reach this goal. Choice A is wrong because the text doesn't focus on her enjoying one unusual topic; it admits some books were a struggle.

The investors and enthusiasts predict books will be replaced by new media. The underlined portion pushes back by pointing out that interactive texts are much older than they assume, going back to notes scribbled in margins, which undercuts their view of books as outdated. It doesn't explain the basis of the technologists' claim; it challenges it.

After the colon, the text says the ensemble helped compose the piece and must be included in every performance, so their participation is essential, or integral. "Tangential" means only loosely connected, which is the opposite of what the text describes.

The conventional wisdom assumes phytoplankton species compete directly, so one should eventually win out. Behrenfeld's team argues that because phytoplankton are so tiny and spread out, direct competition happens much less than people thought, so the conventional view rests on a misconception. Text 2 doesn't mention nutrient replenishment, larger organisms, or competition increasing with density.

Alice's plan sounds excellent and "neatly and simply arranged," meaning it seems easy and uncomplicated, until the narrator notes she has no idea how to carry it out. "Easily" fits. "Foolishly" is tempting given the irony, but the phrase describes how the plan sounds, which is straightforward rather than foolish.

The third sentence states a general principle: links between predators and prey can last across centuries and continents. The rest of the text gives a specific example, since beetles reintroduced after two centuries quickly attacked 93 percent of the mimosa trees. Choice A is wrong because the text never says Chang's team set out to test this idea; they had simply been monitoring the trees.

The text first explains a problem: the written sources by European colonizers underestimate Choctaw women's power. It then describes Pesantubbee's solution, which is using oral tradition and archaeology to supplement those sources. Choice A is wrong because she supplements the written record rather than avoiding it.

The site is described as having yielded a vast diversity of fossils, so it has been very productive, or fruitful. "Obscure" and "unassailable" aren't supported by the description, and "quantified" doesn't describe a rich fossil site.

Birds in dense vegetation sing at lower frequencies because high-frequency sounds don't travel as far there, so the vegetation must reduce, or diminish, that distance. "Exceed" would mean the sounds travel farther, which would give no reason to sing lower. "Conceal" doesn't describe shortening a distance.

Because of how the games handle this information, advocates want to expand players' knowledge of data collection, which means the games are unclear, or opaque, about it. "Outspoken" would mean the games openly explain their practices, the opposite of what the text implies.

The text begins with a view many archaeologists hold, that big engineering projects needed an elite class, and then describes the Alabama canal built by a society with few social classes, which complicates that view. Radiocarbon dating is mentioned, but the text doesn't compare methods.

Gilliam explored a new style by making, or creating, quilt-like paintings inspired by patchwork quilting. "Refusing" and "hiding" contradict the idea of exploring a style, and "predicting" doesn't make sense with paintings.

The text summarizes what the researchers found (the ants treat infected wounds, cutting mortality by 90%) and then points to a possible future use: developing new antibiotics for humans. That matches summarizing findings and then identifying an area for further research. The text doesn't explain the study's methods or how the behavior evolved.

Max has begged his father for as long as he can remember to take him to La Reina, imagines being a hero for crossing its gates, and hopes this summer will finally be the time. The text shows how much he wants to visit. It says nothing about his father's pride or Max disliking summer.

Maize looks so unlike any wild plant that genetic research was needed to establish for certain that teosinte is its ancestor, which is what "confirm" means. Researchers couldn't "develop" or "acquire" a plant as an ancestor.

The team took advantage of the way metals' magnetic fields change under stress, measuring those changes from a distance to find stress in buried pipes. Making use of a property for a purpose is "exploiting" it. "Hypothesized" is tempting, but the team used a known tendency rather than proposing it, and "discounted" means they ignored it.

The statistical analysis confirmed the signal with over 99% confidence, ruling out claims that the event was unclear or open to other interpretations, which is what "ambiguity" means. "Probability" doesn't work, since confirming the signal would support, not preclude, claims that it was likely real.

The claim ignores several recent discoveries and would need to address them to be convincing, so it is weak and poorly supported, or tenuous. "Unoriginal" is a different criticism that the text doesn't make, and "nuanced" is praise that contradicts the text.

Right after saying "Day by day, Dot grew stronger," the underlined sentence gives a concrete example: Dot bounces for hours in her stroller to build her leg muscles. It's a detail showing her growing strength. The behavior is Dot's, not Celestine's, so choice D is wrong.

The word "rather" contrasts the blank with the idea that the accessory spleen "may actively support" diving. So researchers think its role isn't inactive or hidden, which is what "latent" means. "Operative" means active, the opposite of what's needed.
